title: Job Interviews
short: Arrive a few minutes early, dress a step above the job's usual dress, greet everyone kindly, listen, ask good questions, and send a thank-you within a day.
trouble: Learners are polite to the interviewer but curt with the receptionist. Everyone you meet may be asked what they thought of you.

blocks.html: A job interview puts many skills from this course to work at once: small talk, greetings, listening and a thank-you note. For the practical side of finding and applying for a job, see Apply for a Job in Being an Adult.
Arrive a few minutes early, dress a step above the job's usual dress, greet everyone kindly, listen, ask good questions, and send a thank-you within a day.

An interview is a short glimpse of what working with you would be like. Being early shows that you respect the interviewer's schedule. Dressing a step up shows you took the meeting seriously. Kindness to everyone, from the front desk to the interviewer, shows how you treat people when you are not trying to impress them, and a prompt thank-you shows follow-through.

blocks.name: et-order

opts.title: An interview day
items: Learn about the company and plan your questions
Greet the receptionist warmly and give your name
Stand, smile and shake hands with the interviewer
Ask one or two good questions
Send a thank-you email or note within a day

blocks.cap: Put the steps of an interview in order.

blocks.title: The waiting room
blocks.q: Sam arrives for an interview and the receptionist is on the phone. What should he do?
steps: He waits quietly until she is free, without leaning over the desk.
Then he says, "Good morning, I'm Sam Rivera. I have a ten o'clock interview with Ms. Shah."
He thanks her, sits, and keeps his phone silenced.
blocks.a: Wait, greet her kindly, and give his name.

blocks.title: A good question
blocks.q: At the end of her interview, Hana is asked, "Do you have any questions for us?" Which is better: "How much vacation do I get?" or "What does a typical week look like on this team?"
steps: Pay and vacation are fair topics, but they usually come after an offer.
A question about the work shows interest in the job itself.
blocks.a: "What does a typical week look like on this team?"

blocks.name: et-note

parts.subject: Thank you for today's interview
parts.body: Thank you for meeting with me today about the assistant position. I enjoyed hearing about the team's new project, and I would be glad to help with it.

blocks.cap: A thank-you email after an interview.

blocks.html: Being polite to the interviewer but curt with the receptionist. Everyone you meet may be asked what they thought of you. Quick check: would you be glad if the front desk described how you acted in the waiting room?
